messages.content: How should asymptomatic elevated blood pressure (including markedly elevated BP ≥180/110 mm Hg) be managed in the inpatient setting?
Avoid treatment of asymptomatic elevated inpatient BP (including asymptomatic markedly elevated BP, i.e., SBP/DBP ≥180/110 mm Hg) in most situations.
What counseling recommendation should be given to adults to reduce their risk of stroke regarding their physical activity patterns?

In adults, counseling to avoid excessive time spent in sedentary behavior (characterized by low-energy expenditure while sitting, reclining, or lying while awake) is recommended to reduce the risk of stroke.
What type of EEG monitoring should be performed in post-cardiac arrest patients who are unable to follow commands?
Spot electroencephalography (EEG), rather than continuous EEG, can be performed in post-cardiac arrest patients who are unable to follow commands.
How should permanent contraception procedures be categorized in terms of medical necessity and timing?
Permanent contraception should be considered a medically indicated, time-sensitive procedure rather than an elective one.
What surveillance strategy should NOT be used for detection of recurrence in patients who have undergone curative-intent treatment of stage I-III NSCLC or SCLC?
Clinicians should not use circulating biomarkers as a surveillance strategy for detection of recurrence in patients who have undergone curative-intent treatment of stage I-III NSCLC or SCLC.
What is the recommendation regarding the use of opioids for treating breathlessness in people with serious respiratory illness?
Opioids should not be used for the treatment of breathlessness in people with serious respiratory illness.
What should clinicians use to counsel patients with a detectable PSA about their risk of clinical progression?

Clinicians should use prognostic factors (e.g., PSA doubling time, Gleason Grade Group, pathologic stage, surgical margin status, validated post-prostatectomy genomic classifier and/or positron emission tomography imaging results) to counsel patients with a detectable PSA about their risk of clinical progression.
How should diphtheria antitoxin be administered in patients with suspected or confirmed symptomatic diphtheria?

Administer a single dose of diphtheria antitoxin with choice of dose based on disease severity and time since symptom onset, in comparison with a fixed dose for all patients, in patients with suspected or confirmed symptomatic diphtheria.
In what clinical settings and circumstances should darkfield microscopy be maintained for syphilis diagnosis?

Darkfield microscopy should be maintained if already in use or established in sexually transmitted diseases clinics where a point-of-care test for primary or secondary syphilis diagnosis would be beneficial for timely patient treatment.
What is the recommended approach for managing patients with evidence of pelvic lymph node recurrence after radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy?

Clinicians may offer salvage pelvic lymphadenectomy for patients with evidence of pelvic lymph node recurrence after radical prostatectomy (RP) or radiotherapy (RT), but should counsel patients on the uncertain oncologic benefit from surgery in this setting.
What should be done with FIO2 during an SBT?
FIO2 (Fraction of Inspired Oxygen) should not be increased during an SBT.
What vitamin D supplementation dosing strategy is recommended for patients?
Low daily doses of vitamin D supplementation are recommended over high doses given at intervals such as weekly or monthly.
What approach may clinicians take for initial evaluation of patients with symptoms suggestive of OAB, and what are the associated requirements regarding physical exam and urinalysis?

Clinicians may offer telemedicine to initially evaluate patients with symptoms suggestive of OAB, with the understanding that a physical exam will not be performed and urinalysis should be obtained at a local laboratory (or recent lab results reviewed, if available).
What imaging modality should clinicians avoid using as a surveillance tool for lung cancer recurrence?
Clinicians should not use 18F-labeled fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography as a surveillance tool for lung cancer recurrence.
What abortive medications should clinicians use in the prodromal phase of CHS?
In the prodromal phase of CHS, clinicians should use triptans, H1-antihistamines, or benzodiazepines as abortive medications.
What is the minimum number of positive and negative tissues that laboratories should test for initial analytic validation of nonpredictive laboratory-developed assays?
For initial analytic validation of nonpredictive laboratory-developed assays, laboratories should test a minimum of 10 positive and 10 negative tissues.
What supplementation is recommended for adults aged 75 and older?
Empirical vitamin D supplementation is recommended for adults aged 75 and older.
What classification system is recommended for use as a reporting standard of disease extent in patients with aortic dissection?
In patients with aortic dissection, Ishimaru zones are recommended for use as a reporting standard of disease extent.
How should endpoint titers be determined and reported when testing serum with nontreponemal (lipoidal antigen) assays that detect antibodies to lipoidal antigens?

Endpoint titers should be determined and clearly reported when testing serum with nontreponemal (lipoidal antigen) assays that detect antibodies to lipoidal antigens. Reports should not contain mathematical symbols such as > or < signs.
What is recommended for patients with chronic symptomatic PAD to improve walking performance, functional status, and QOL?
In patients with chronic symptomatic PAD, SET is recommended to improve walking performance, functional status, and QOL.
What are the requirements for initial analytic verification of unmodified FDA-approved predictive marker assays in laboratories?

For initial analytic verification of all unmodified FDA-approved predictive marker assays, laboratories should follow the specific instructions provided by the manufacturer. If the package insert does not delineate specific instructions for assay verification, the laboratory should test a minimum of 20 positive and 20 negative tissues.
What treatment should be considered to induce remission in individual patients with non-EoE EGIDs after thorough discussion of benefits and risks with the patient and parents?

The use of oral systemic steroids should be considered to induce remission in individual patients with non-EoE EGIDs after thorough discussion with the patient and parents about their benefits and risks.
When should an experienced genitourinary pathologist review a patient's pathology?

An experienced genitourinary pathologist should review the pathology of a patient with any doubt regarding variant or suspected variant histology, extensive squamous or glandular differentiation, or the presence/absence of lymphovascular invasion.
How should nontreponemal and treponemal tests be interpreted in relation to a patient's HIV status?
Nontreponemal and treponemal tests should be interpreted in the same manner regardless of HIV status.
What intervention should be used to reduce breathlessness in people with serious respiratory illness?
Increased airflow should be used to reduce breathlessness in people with serious respiratory illness.
What is the preferred treatment for rhodesiense human African trypanosomiasis in patients ≥6 years of age and weighing ≥20 kg?
Fexinidazole is the preferred treatment for rhodesiense human African trypanosomiasis in patients ≥6 years of age and weighing ≥20 kg.
What specific expertise should at least one clinician member of a responding Rapid Response Team possess?

At least one clinician member of a responding Rapid Response Team should have expertise in eliciting patients' goals of care and establishing treatment plans that reflect patients' wishes and prognosis.
How should the quantity of DoxyPEP be determined when writing prescriptions for interested patients?
Patients interested in DoxyPEP should receive a prescription for the expected number of doses until the next visit.
What medications and supplements should be prescribed for patients in the inter-episodic phase of CHS, and what is the minimal effective dosing for TCAs?

In the inter-episodic phase of CHS, clinicians should use tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs; e.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline), anticonvulsants, and mitochondrial supplements (e.g., vitamin B2, coenzyme Q10), with a minimal effective dosing of TCAs thought to be 75 mg to 100 mg of amitriptyline.
What screening procedure is recommended for PLHIV younger than 35 who have anal symptoms or abnormalities on digital examination, regardless of history of anal intercourse?
For PLHIV younger than 35 who have anal symptoms or abnormalities on digital examination, standard anoscopy is recommended regardless of history of anal intercourse.
What type of system should hospitals deploy for non-ICU patients, and what components should this system include?
Hospitals should deploy rapid response systems (i.e., RRT/MET) for non-ICU patients that include explicit activation criteria for obtaining help from a designated response team.
What should be considered regarding immunosuppressive therapy for patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis who remain on dialysis and have no extrarenal manifestations of disease?
Consider discontinuation of immunosuppressive therapy after 3 months in patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis who remain on dialysis and who do not have any extrarenal manifestations of disease.
What should be the approach regarding postoperative supervised therapy after carpal tunnel release?
Postoperative supervised therapy should not be routinely prescribed after carpal tunnel release.

What are the minimum tissue sample requirements for laboratories performing initial analytic validation of laboratory-developed assays and verification of FDA-approved or cleared predictive immunohistochemical assays with distinct scoring schemes (eg, HER2, PD-L1)?

For initial analytic validation of laboratory-developed assays and verification of FDA-approved or cleared predictive immunohistochemical assays with distinct scoring schemes (eg, HER2, PD-L1), laboratories should separately validate or verify each assay-scoring system combination with a minimum of 20 positive and 20 negative tissues.
How should hemoglobin concentrations be handled with respect to infection and inflammation when diagnosing anemia in individuals and populations?
Haemoglobin concentrations should not be adjusted to diagnose anaemia in individuals and populations to account for the effect of infection and inflammation.
Where and when should patients with high risk of severe illness be seen?
Patients with high risk of severe illness should be seen in an emergency department or equivalent setting as soon as possible.
What standardized daily protocol should be followed regarding assessment and completion of Spontaneous Breathing Trials (SBT)?
A standardized approach to assessment and, if appropriate, completion of an SBT should be performed before noon each day.
What type of imaging should clinicians use for surveillance of lung cancer recurrence during the first two years after treatment?

Clinicians should use a diagnostic or low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) that includes the adrenals, without contrast (preferred) or with contrast (when indicated) when conducting surveillance for recurrence during the first two years post treatment for lung cancer.
How should the aorta be viewed, interpreted and treated in terms of diagnosis, treatment and surveillance?
It is recommended to view, interpret and treat the aorta in the context of an organ, whereby diagnosis, treatment and surveillance should be approached with this perspective.
What cardiac medication should be used as part of pharmacotherapy for patients with obstructive symptomatic HCM?
Cardiac myosin inhibitors, specifically mavacamten, should be used as part of pharmacotherapy for patients with obstructive symptomatic HCM.
In the preoperative evaluation for noncardiac surgery, when should stress testing be considered?

Stress testing should be considered only in select patients with elevated risk and poor or unknown functional capacity if an indication for testing exists independent of planned surgery or if high-risk myocardial ischemia is suspected.
What is the recommended fluid resuscitation protocol for patients with acute pancreatitis?

Moderately aggressive fluid resuscitation with lactated Ringer's solution should be started for patients with acute pancreatitis, defined as a bolus of 10 mL/kg followed by infusion of 1.5 mL/kg/hour, with additional boluses given if a patient has evidence of hypovolemia.
What should be administered to infants and young children for protection against respiratory syncytial virus?
RSV-mAb (nirsevimab) should be administered to infants and young children for protection against respiratory syncytial virus.
What is the recommended approach for managing persistent sacroiliac joint pain that has not responded to conservative measures for 4 weeks?

Image-guided, intra-articular corticosteroid injections are recommended for persistent sacroiliac joint pain that has persisted despite conservative measures for 4 weeks. Fluoroscopic and CT guided injections are the preferred imaging modality of choice, although ultrasound guidance can be considered in situations where radiation exposure may be problematic.
What type of protocol should be used for managing hyperglycemia in critically ill adults receiving IV insulin infusions?
A protocol that includes explicit decision support tools should be used over a protocol with no such tools in critically ill adults receiving IV insulin infusions for the management of hyperglycemia.
In which patients is terlipressin use contraindicated?
Terlipressin use is contraindicated in patients with hypoxemia and in patients with ongoing coronary, peripheral, or mesenteric ischemia.
How should nontreponemal and treponemal tests be interpreted in relation to pregnancy status?
Nontreponemal and treponemal tests should be interpreted in the same manner regardless of pregnancy status.
What therapy formats should not be used as primary treatments for PTSD?
Group, marital, or family therapy formats should not be used as primary treatments for PTSD.
How should patients with Behçet disease be monitored following their diagnosis?
Patients with Behçet disease should be monitored closely for complications during the first year following diagnosis due to increased mortality risk.
For which HIV status groups is DoxyPEP appropriate?
DoxyPEP is appropriate for both people living with HIV and those without HIV.
In which patients is it reasonable to use an Lp(a) ≥125 nmol/L or ≥50 mg/dL as a risk-enhancing factor to favor initiation of a moderate- or high-intensity statin?

In adults aged 40–75 y with a 10-y ASCVD risk of 7.5%–19.9%, an Lp(a) ≥125 nmol/L or ≥50 mg/dL is reasonable to use as a risk-enhancing factor to favor initiation of a moderate- or high-intensity statin in those with on-treatment LDL-C ≥ 70 mg/dL (or non-HDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL).
What diagnostic tool can be used to diagnose carpal tunnel syndrome in lieu of routine Ultrasonography or NCV/EMG?
CTS-6 can be used to diagnose carpal tunnel syndrome, in lieu of routine use of Ultrasonography or NCV/EMG.
What is the current classification of Bictegravir/FTC/TAF for initial HIV therapy during pregnancy?
Bictegravir/FTC/TAF is now considered an alternative for initial HIV therapy during pregnancy.

When resources are constrained, which radiation therapy patients should be prioritized for prophylactic management of lymphoedema over patients who receive radiation to the breast/chest wall ± the supraclavicular fossa?

Patients who received axillary radiation should be prioritized for prophylactic management of lymphoedema over patients who receive radiation to the breast/chest wall ± the supraclavicular fossa when resources are constrained.

What therapy should be added for patients with heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥40 percent who are receiving optimal therapy but have persistent New York Heart Association class II to III HF symptoms?

In patients with heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥40 percent receiving optimal therapy with persistent New York Heart Association class II to III HF symptoms, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) should be added.
What two clinical assessments should be performed at each occurrence/recurrence of bladder cancer?
At the time of each occurrence/recurrence of bladder cancer, assign a clinical stage and classify the patient as "low-," "intermediate-," or "high-risk."
What should be performed as the first diagnostic study in hemodynamically unstable patients with lower gastrointestinal bleeding?
CTA should be performed as the first diagnostic study in hemodynamically unstable patients with lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
What type of care approach should be adopted for youth living with HIV?
Trauma-informed care should be adopted for youth (specifically adolescents) living with HIV.
How should patients with moderate risk of severe illness be evaluated?
Patients with moderate risk of severe illness should be seen in an ambulatory setting for in-person evaluation as soon as possible.
How should pathologists validate laboratory-developed tests for PD-L1 expression?
Pathologists who choose to use laboratory-developed tests for PD-L1 expression should validate according to the requirements of their accrediting body.
What guidance should be followed regarding the use of IV albumin for volume replacement and bypass circuit priming in cardiovascular surgery patients?
IV albumin should be avoided in cardiovascular surgery patients for volume replacement or to prime the cardiovascular bypass circuit.
What preoperative biomarker testing should be performed for patients with poor or unknown functional capacity when additional testing might affect decision-making?
For patients with poor or unknown functional capacity, measure preoperative B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal proBNP if further testing might affect decision-making.
After what duration of effective TB treatment should patients be considered non-infectious or at low likelihood of infectiousness, regardless of sputum bacteriologic status?

Persons with TB on effective treatment for at least five days should be considered non-infectious or low likelihood of infectiousness, regardless of sputum bacteriologic status during treatment (i.e., smear-microscopy, NAAT or culture status), with certain exceptions.
What should all epilepsy centers have to provide optimal care?
All epilepsy centers should have physicians with sufficient training and expertise to provide optimal care.
How frequently should atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk be estimated in adults aged 40-79 years, and what is the purpose of this assessment?

In adults 40-79 years of age, estimation of risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ie, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, and fatal CVD) every 1 to 5 years is beneficial to guide decisions on treatments and lifestyle recommendations that may reduce risk for stroke.
What is the initial diagnostic test of choice for PAD in patients with suggestive history or exam findings, and how should the results be reported?

To establish a PAD diagnosis, the resting ankle–brachial index (ABI) is the initial test of choice in patients with suggestive history or exam findings. The ABI result should be reported as normal (1–1.4), borderline (0.91–0.99), abnormal (≤0.9) or noncompressible (>1.4).
What syphilis screening protocol should obstetrician-gynecologists and other obstetric care professionals follow for pregnant individuals?

Obstetrician-gynecologists and other obstetric care professionals should screen all pregnant individuals serologically for syphilis at the first prenatal care visit, followed by universal rescreening during the third trimester and at birth, rather than use a risk-based approach to testing.
What is the long-term effectiveness of PRP injection (leukocyte rich or leukocyte poor) in the non-operative treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome?
PRP Injection does not provide long-term benefits in non-operative treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome (leukocyte rich or leukocyte poor PRP).
What is the recommended breast cancer screening protocol for women aged 40 to 74 who are at average risk for breast cancer?
Biennial screening mammograms are recommended for women aged 40 to 74 who are at average risk for breast cancer.
Under what circumstances should testing for respiratory viruses be performed?
Testing for respiratory viruses should be performed if there is high pretest probability of respiratory viral infection based on clinical presentation and local prevalence.
What medication should be administered to adult patients hospitalized with severe bacterial community-acquired pneumonia?
Administer corticosteroids to adult patients hospitalized with severe bacterial community-acquired pneumonia.
How should testing for respiratory viruses be performed?
Testing for respiratory viruses should be performed following FDA-approved manufacturers' recommendations.
What screening is recommended for asymptomatic adults ≥18 years of age who have overweight, obesity, or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease to inform stroke risk?
In asymptomatic adults ≥18 years of age who have overweight, obesity, or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, screening for prediabetes and diabetes is recommended to inform stroke risk.
What imaging protocol should clinicians follow when diagnosing and planning treatment for sacroiliac joint dysfunction?

Clinicians should obtain appropriate imaging and rule out other pathologies such as fracture, malignancy, and spinal disease when diagnosing sacroiliac joint dysfunction. If planning surgical treatment, advanced imaging such as CT or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) should be performed within 12 months or with any change in symptomatology.
In which patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis should plasma exchange be considered?

Consider plasma exchange for patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis with serum creatinine >3.4 mg/dl, patients requiring dialysis or with rapidly increasing serum creatinine, or patients with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage who have hypoxemia.
What specific services and requirements must SMA specialty care centers provide when accepting newborn screening referrals?

Every SMA specialty care center accepting SMA newborn screening referrals should provide prompt initial evaluation within 2 days, follow-up visits, access to treatment options, confirmatory diagnostic testing, education and resources for caregivers, and coordination with primary care provider and other specialists.
For patients with high-risk features, what is the recommended duration for extending ADT?
For patients with high-risk features, clinicians may extend ADT to 18 to 24 months.
What components should be included in all standard TNE studies, and what additional measurement may be considered?
All standard TNE studies should include transmitral flow (E/A ratio, IVRT) and a measure of LA size. Measurement of pulmonary vein velocities may be considered.
What level of concordance should laboratories achieve between a new assay and the comparator assay or expected results during initial analytic validation or verification of clinically used assays?

For initial analytic validation or verification of every assay used clinically, laboratories should achieve at least 90% overall concordance between the new assay and the comparator assay or expected results.
What considerations should be made when administering influenza vaccines to persons with egg allergy of any severity?
Persons with egg allergy of any severity can receive any appropriate influenza vaccine without special considerations.
What measurement is reasonable to perform in all adults to refine risk assessment for ASCVD events?
Measurement of Lp(a) in all adults is reasonable to refine risk assessment for ASCVD events.
How should clinicians diagnose cannabis hyperemesis syndrome (CHS)?

Clinicians should diagnose cannabis hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) based on episodic vomiting occurring ≥3 times annually, cannabis use for >1 year before symptom onset (usually >4 times weekly on average), and symptom resolution after cannabis abstinence for at least 6 months or the duration of ≥3 vomiting cycles.
What should be done regarding antifungal therapy when there is persistent presence of cryptococcal antigen in blood or cerebrospinal fluid?
Antifungal therapy should not be escalated for persistent presence of cryptococcal antigen in blood or cerebrospinal fluid.
What may clinicians offer to patients with BCR following RP without any high-risk features?
For patients with BCR following RP without any high-risk features, clinicians may offer radiation alone.
What therapy is recommended for patients with symptomatic PAD to reduce the risk of MACE?
In patients with symptomatic PAD, single antiplatelet therapy is recommended to reduce the risk of MACE.
What should be included in all standard TNE assessments, and what specific measures should be included in PDA evaluation?
All standard TNE should include an assessment for the presence and directionality of shunts. Evaluation of the PDA should include measures of LA volume loading and SBF.
How frequently should STI testing be performed for patients using DoxyPEP?
STI testing should be performed at baseline and 3- to 6-month intervals for patients using DoxyPEP.
With which patients should doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis (DoxyPEP) be discussed?

Doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis (DoxyPEP) should be discussed with men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women (TGW) who have had a bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI) within the past 12 months.
What type of education should be provided to direct-care non-ICU hospital clinicians?
Focused education of direct-care non-ICU hospital clinicians on recognizing early clinical deterioration should be provided.
What treatment options should clinicians offer for patients in whom salvage local therapy is being considered following focal ablation?
Clinicians should offer whole gland treatment by radical prostatectomy (RP) or radiotherapy (RT) for patients in whom salvage local therapy is being considered following focal ablation.
How should antifungal therapy regimens for cryptococcosis be managed once optimized?
Antifungal therapy regimens for cryptococcosis should remain optimized and not be changed needlessly.
What are the recommended imaging modalities for the diagnostic assessment of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD)?
In the diagnostic assessment of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD), conventional radiography (CR) and ultrasound (or CT if axial involvement is suspected) are recommended imaging modalities.
What antiretroviral regimen is recommended for pregnant people who have received long-acting injectable cabotegravir for preexposure prophylaxis?
Ritonavir-boosted darunavir plus dual NRTIs is recommended for pregnant people who have received long-acting injectable cabotegravir for preexposure prophylaxis.
What measurements should be routinely performed, and what imaging should be done when ductal shunt significance is in question?
LVO should be routinely measured. Imaging to determine the diastolic flow direction centrally and peripherally should be performed where ductal shunt significance is in question.
Which individuals should receive the Mpox vaccine (Jynneos)?
Mpox vaccine (Jynneos) should be administered to high-risk individuals aged 18 years.
What should obstetrician-gynecologists and other obstetric health care professionals consider when pregnant individuals present with symptoms of respiratory illness?

Obstetrician–gynecologists and other obstetric health care professionals should consider both influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infection for pregnant individuals who present with symptoms of respiratory illness.
Which diagnostic tests should not be used to diagnose carpal tunnel syndrome?
MRI and Upper Limb Neurodynamic Testing should not be used to diagnose carpal tunnel syndrome.
For which severe ARDS patients should venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) be used?
Use venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for select patients with severe ARDS (PaO2:FiO2 <80 or pH <7.25 with PaCO2 ≥60 mm Hg).
For which high-risk patients with FH and ASCVD is lipoprotein apheresis considered reasonable?

Lipoprotein apheresis is reasonable for high-risk patients with FH and ASCVD (coronary or peripheral arteries) whose Lp(a) level remains ≥60 mg/dL (∼150 nmol/L) and LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL on maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy.
What should clinicians recommend regarding the addition of docetaxel in patients undergoing salvage RT and ADT?
Clinicians should not recommend the addition of docetaxel in patients undergoing salvage RT and ADT.
What should be included in all standard TNE evaluations?

All standard TNE evaluations should include an assessment of the position of any central lines, an exclusion of pericardial effusion, and surveillance for potential complications such as thrombosis and/or vegetations.
How should the relative infectiousness of persons with TB be considered based on their duration of effective treatment?
Persons with TB on less than five days of effective treatment should be considered relatively more infectious than those on longer durations of effective therapy.
What COVID-19 vaccination products are recommended for both primary series and boosters?
COVID-19 vaccination with current monovalent 2023–2024 products is recommended for both primary series and boosters.
What should be done regarding IV albumin administration in patients with cirrhosis and extraperitoneal infections?
IV albumin should be avoided in patients with cirrhosis and extraperitoneal infections.
What screening recommendation is given for adults ≥18 years of age to reduce their risk of stroke?
In individuals ≥18 years of age, periodic screening for modifiable behaviors and medical conditions that increase stroke risk is recommended to reduce risk for stroke.
What alternative to autoinjectors should be considered for anaphylaxis treatment in children and adults weighing ≥30 kg?
Epinephrine nasal spray (neffy) should be considered as an alternative to autoinjectors for anaphylaxis treatment in children and adults weighing ≥30 kg.
What should be used to reduce symptoms in people with serious respiratory illness?
Breathing techniques should be used to reduce symptoms in people with serious respiratory illness.

What diagnostic procedure should clinicians perform to evaluate for local recurrence in patients with biochemical recurrence following primary radiotherapy or ablative therapy who have no evidence of metastatic disease and are candidates for local salvage therapy?

Clinicians should perform a prostate biopsy to evaluate for local recurrence in patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR) following primary radiotherapy (RT) or ablative therapy who have no evidence of metastatic disease and are candidates for local salvage therapy.
What type of screening is beneficial for identifying additional factors that contribute to stroke risk in individuals ≥18 years of age?

In individuals ≥18 years of age, periodic screening for social determinants of health (eg, food insecurity, lack of transportation) is beneficial to identify additional factors that contribute to stroke risk.
When is susceptibility testing advised for Helicobacter pylori infection?
Susceptibility testing is advised when choice of salvage therapy for persistent Helicobacter pylori infection is unclear.
What is the recommended surveillance imaging schedule for monitoring recurrence in patients after curative treatment for lung cancer?
Patients should undergo surveillance imaging for recurrence every six months for two years after curative treatment for lung cancer.
What is the recommended daily protein intake for adults with CKD stages G3-G5?
Maintain a protein intake of 0.8 g/kg body weight/d in adults with CKD G3–G5.
What supplementation is recommended for adults with high-risk prediabetes?
Empirical vitamin D supplementation is recommended for adults with high-risk prediabetes.

What brain MRI surveillance schedule should be offered to patients who have undergone curative-intent treatment of stage I-III SCLC, regardless of whether they received prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI)?

In patients who have undergone curative-intent treatment of stage I-III SCLC and did not receive prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI), clinicians should offer brain MRI every three months for the first year and every six months for the second year for surveillance. The same schedule may be offered for patients who did receive PCI.
In which youth patient population is selective screening of Lp(a) recommended?
Selective screening of Lp(a) is recommended in high-risk youth (aged <18 y) patients.
What imaging modalities should be used to monitor gout, and what aspects can they assess?

In gout, ultrasound and DECT can be used to monitor crystal deposition and in case of ultrasound, also inflammation. Both modalities provide additional information on top of clinical and biochemical assessment. In case ultrasound/DECT are not available, CR can be used to assess structural damage due to gout.
What treatment should clinicians offer to patients with pelvic nodal recurrence following primary RT who did not receive prior pelvic nodal RT?

Clinicians should offer salvage pelvic nodal radiotherapy (RT) plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for patients with pelvic nodal recurrence following primary RT who did not receive prior pelvic nodal RT.
Are influenza vaccines manufactured with eggs safe for patients with egg allergies, and if so, for which patients?
Influenza vaccines manufactured with eggs are safe for all users, including those with egg allergies.
What approach to supplemental oxygen should be considered for symptom reduction in people with serious respiratory illness?
Either administering or not administering supplemental oxygen may be considered to reduce symptoms in people with serious respiratory illness.
When can synovial fluid analysis be omitted in confirming a diagnosis of gout?

When characteristic features of monosodium urate (MSU) crystal deposition on ultrasound (i.e., double-contour sign or tophi) or on DECT are identified, synovial fluid analysis is not needed to confirm a diagnosis of gout.
What suture width and interval should be used for continuous closure of a midline laparotomy incision in patients with BMI ≤30 kg/m2?

For patients with body mass index (BMI) ≤30 kg/m2 undergoing continuous closure of a midline laparotomy incision, use a 5 mm suture width and interval rather than the conventional technique of 10 mm suture width and interval.
When should Abrysvo RSV vaccine be administered during pregnancy to induce antibodies in neonates?
Abrysvo RSV vaccine is recommended in the last month of pregnancy to induce antibodies in neonates.
What COVID-19 preexposure prophylaxis measures should be provided for children with HIV?

COVID-19 preexposure prophylaxis should be provided for children with HIV, including vaccination for all those aged ≥6 months and monoclonal antibody for those aged ≥12 years with severe immunosuppression.
When should Doppler tissue imaging be included in TNE assessment and considered for evaluation of heart function?

Where normative data exist, Doppler tissue imaging should be included in a standard TNE assessment as part of a multiparametric appraisal of heart function. Myocardial velocities should be considered when there is suspected heart dysfunction and disagreement between other modalities.
What should be added to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control?

Add a sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist to metformin and lifestyle modifications in adults with type 2 diabetes and inadequate glycemic control.
What are the testing requirements for laboratory-developed assays that have both predictive and nonpredictive applications using the same scoring criteria?

For laboratory-developed assays with both predictive and nonpredictive applications using the same scoring criteria, laboratories should treat these assays as predictive markers and test a minimum of 20 positive and 20 negative cases.
What should medical floor staff do when a patient exhibits any cause for concern?

When a medical floor patient exhibits any cause for concern, staff should immediately acquire a new, complete set of vital signs and report substantial abnormalities to appropriate clinicians urgently.
What components should be included in all standard TNE studies?
All standard TNE studies should include continuous-wave Doppler of any TR and/or PI jet, systolic EI, and evaluation of PA Doppler waveform for PVR index and the presence of notching.
What is the haemoglobin cutoff value that should be used for defining anaemia in children 6-23 months of age?
The haemoglobin cutoff for defining anaemia in children 6-23 months of age should be <105 g/L.
What interventions can be considered in patients with acute isolated meniscal tears undergoing surgical repair to improve outcomes?
Bone Marrow Venting or Platelet Rich Plasma can be considered in patients with acute isolated meniscal tears undergoing surgical repair to improve outcomes.
What is the recommended use of neuromuscular blockade in patients with severe ARDS?
Use neuromuscular blockade (NMB) in early treatment of patients with severe ARDS (partial pressure of oxygen [PaO2]:fraction of inspired oxygen [FiO2] <100) for 48 hours or less.

What level of pain relief should patients experience with an appropriately performed local anesthetic only injection to diagnose sacroiliac joint dysfunction, and how should this relief relate to the anesthetic used?

Patients should experience greater than 50% relief when an appropriately performed local anesthetic only injection is completed that is consistent with duration of the local anesthetic utilized for diagnosing sacroiliac joint dysfunction.
What type of validation tissues should laboratories use when testing clinical cases?
Laboratories should use validation tissues that have been processed using the same fixative and processing methods as cases that will be tested clinically, when possible.
What is the preferred diagnostic strategy that should be performed prior to neuroablative procedures of the sacroiliac joint?

Dual diagnostic blockade of the L5 primary dorsal ramus and sacral lateral branches (S1-3) with 50% improvement in pain and function is the preferred strategy prior to neuroablative procedures of the sacroiliac joint.

What is the recommendation regarding postoperative radiotherapy for patients who have undergone surgery for bone metastases in either non-spine locations or in the spine without spinal cord or cauda equina compression?
Postoperative RT is recommended for patients who have undergone surgery for non-spine bone metastases or for spine metastases without spinal cord or cauda equina compression.
What should be obtained prior to digital anorectal examination for anal cancer screening?
Laboratory tests for anal cancer screening should be obtained prior to digital anorectal examination.
What test or measurement is not needed to determine readiness for a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?
An RSBI (Rapid Shallow Breathing Index) is not needed to determine readiness for an SBT (Spontaneous Breathing Trial).

What treatment is recommended as an alternative to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor for patients ≥12 years of age with WHIM syndrome due to a confirmed CXCR4 variant who have significant lymphopenia and related infections?

Mavorixafor is recommended as an alternative to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor for patients ≥12 years of age with WHIM syndrome due to a confirmed CXCR4 variant who have significant lymphopenia and related infections.
How should hypertensive emergency be managed according to current clinical practice guidelines?
Manage hypertensive emergency as recommended in the 2017 multisociety hypertension clinical practice guideline.
